subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Horizon Medical)

Date: 2027-06-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Horizon Medical)

Hi Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of pain points
- Peak inference latency spikes during morning batch processing window (45–60k requests/min) causing client timeouts.
- PHI isolation & auditability requirement — need VPC-level network isolation, customer-managed KMS, and 1yr+ audit log retention.
- Predictable pricing for high-volume LLM usage; procurement needs a clear billing cadence and SLA.

Goals we heard
- Dedicated GPU capacity (reserved pool) to guarantee throughput for core clinical pipelines.
- Isolation: VPC + no co-tenancy for workloads processing PHI.
- Autoscale/burst plan to handle 2x peak for bi-weekly reporting windows.
- SLA target of 99.95% availability; RTO/RPO for critical endpoints.

Proposed Redwood configuration (high-level)
- Reserved pool: 8x H100-equivalent GPU nodes (can map to H100 or A100 depending on procurement), isolated in a dedicated cluster.
- Warm pool / burst: 4x on-demand nodes attached with fast warm-up to support 2x peak for 30–60 min bursts.
- Network: customer VPC peering, private control plane, KMS integration for keys, audit logs shipped to your S3 (or our secure log delivery) with 1yr retention.
- SLAs: we can commit to 99.95% platform availability on Dedicated with credits for breaches; Ops playbook for incident response and 24/7 escalation path.

Next steps
1) Technical deep dive with Marissa to finalize VM/GPU sizing and network diagram — propose Tue 6/22 or Wed 6/23.
2) Share a draft dedicated capacity proposal + preliminary pricing (attached).
3) Security/compliance questionnaire — we’ll have our SOC 2 info and audit logs sample ready for your security team.
4) Procurement timeline: if you can confirm by end of next week we can target a July go-live for the reserved pool.

Attachments: dedicated-capacity-proposal.pdf (high-level config + pricing), network-architecture.png (example VPC topology).

If this aligns, I’ll lock in the meeting with Marissa and send a tailored quote + draft MSA.

Thanks — Ben

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Burst behavior: during reporting windows some jobs are very short but fan out to multiple models. We want to ensure the KV cache and batching don’t cause cold-starts that spike latency. Is the warm pool sticky to session warmed caches or do we need an explicit pre-warm process?
- Audit logs: 1yr retention is fine. Can you confirm log format and whether we can ship directly to our S3 with requester-pays turned off?
- SLA: 99.95% is acceptable but procurement will want to see the credit schedule and any exclusions (maintenance windows, force majeure).

Procurement note: we’re aiming to approve the vendor stack by 7/8 to start work mid-July. I’ll loop in procurement if we get the pricing and MSA draft.

Also please include pricing tiers for option A (H100) vs option B (A100) — we’ll run headcount across both.

—Sam

Hi Sam — great to meet today. A few technical clarifications to address your questions: 

1) Warm pool & KV cache
- Our warm pool is designed to maintain loaded model weights and KV cache for a subset of active sessions. For workloads that need session affinity (long-lived chats or interactive sessions) we recommend sticky routing to the reserved pool. For your batched jobs, we can pre-warm using a short synthetic traffic pattern (scripted warm-up) before the reporting window; we’ll include that in runbook.

2) Burst capacity semantics
- Burst nodes join the same cluster but are tagged as preemptible to reduce cost if you want. They will have access to the same cache layer; however, cold cache misses can still occur for rare contexts. We can configure a TTL-based proactive pre-warm for critical prompts.

3) Network / logs / KMS
- We support direct delivery to your S3 (PutObject) with configurable prefixes and encryption metadata. Requester-pays can be disabled on our side — we’ll confirm exact IAM role and bucket policy in the architecture doc.

4) GPU options & perf implications
- H100: best perf for FP16 and FP8 mixed workloads, reduces latency by ~20–30% vs A100 on our benchmarks for dense LLMs.
- A100: lower capital cost, slightly higher tail latency. We’ll provide both pricing options and a recommended mapping based on your token/sec needs.

I attached a short proposal + network diagram with recommended sizing and a suggested autoscale policy (min 8 reserved, max 12 with 4 burst).

Happy to run a perf sim against a sample prompt set if you can share a small subset of prompts/seq lengths (can be sanitized). Proposed times for the technical deep-dive: Tue 2027-06-22 10:00 AM PT or Wed 2027-06-23 11:00 AM PT. Which works best?

Cheers,
